blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Media, Communication, Arts & Design
QUALIFICATION
Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies
Media, Communication & Culture
CAREER LEVEL
Entry-level
Brand Executive / Marketing Associate / Junior Brand Manager

A Junior Brand Manager helps develop and maintain a brand's identity, positioning, reputation, and market presence. The role combines consumer understanding, creative communication, marketing strategy, campaign coordination, and performance analysis.

A degree in Media, Communication & Culture can provide a useful foundation in storytelling, audience behaviour, media platforms, cultural trends, and communication strategy. Students can complement this foundation with marketing, business, consumer research, and digital analytics skills.
Junior brand professionals commonly work with marketing managers, designers, advertising agencies, sales teams, product teams, and external partners to deliver consistent brand experiences.

Career progression
Some employers use “Assistant Brand Manager” or “Brand Executive” for early-career roles. Responsibilities and entry requirements differ across industries.
Year 1
Foundation
Understand communication and audiences

items.text: Study media studies, communication theory, culture, and audience behaviour.
Learn marketing fundamentals, branding concepts, and consumer psychology.
Practise copywriting, storytelling, and presentation skills.
Analyse how different brands communicate across platforms.
Learn basic Excel or Google Sheets and presentation design.
Maintain a record of interesting campaigns and explain why they work.

blocks.text: Year 2
Core skills
Learn brand and marketing execution

items.text: Study brand positioning, brand identity, segmentation, and target audiences.
Learn consumer research, competitor analysis, and customer journey mapping.
Understand digital marketing, social media strategy, and content calendars.
Learn campaign planning, basic budgeting, and performance measurement.
Explore tools such as Canva, Google Analytics, and advertising dashboards.
Create a mock brand strategy for a product or service.

blocks.text: Year 3
Application
Build a brand portfolio

items.text: Create a brand positioning statement and communication plan.
Develop a campaign concept with audience insights and creative direction.
Practise analysing campaign performance and recommending improvements.
Complete an internship with a brand, agency, startup, or marketing team.
Collaborate with designers, content creators, and digital marketers.
Document projects with objectives, decisions, deliverables, and outcomes.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for recruitment

items.text: Complete a capstone brand strategy or integrated marketing campaign.
Learn to prepare campaign briefs, marketing budgets, and performance reports.
Practise presenting strategic recommendations to stakeholders.
Develop a portfolio with two or three well-explained case studies.
Apply for brand executive, marketing associate, and assistant brand manager roles.
Consider postgraduate study if it aligns with your career plans.

blocks.text: Adapt this roadmap to the programme's duration and curriculum. A three-year degree can cover the same competencies on a compressed schedule.
A. Brand Strategy
Develops brand positioning, differentiation, value propositions, and long-term brand direction.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Consumer insights, competitor analysis, positioning, brand architecture.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Brand Executive, Junior Brand Strategist, Assistant Brand Manager.
B. Integrated Marketing and Campaigns
Coordinates campaigns across advertising, digital media, events, public relations, and other channels.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Campaign planning, briefing agencies, scheduling, budgeting, coordination.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Marketing Associate, Campaign Executive, Brand Communications Executive.
C. Consumer Insights and Brand Analytics
Studies audience needs, brand awareness, customer preferences, and campaign effectiveness.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Surveys, market research, Excel, analytics, performance reporting.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Consumer Insights Analyst, Brand Research Executive, Marketing Analyst.
D. Digital and Social Brand Management
Builds a brand's online presence through content, social platforms, creator partnerships, and digital campaigns.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Content strategy, social analytics, digital advertising, creator coordination.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Digital Marketing Executive, Social Media Strategist, Digital Brand Associate.
E. Consumer Product and Retail Branding
Supports product launches, packaging, promotions, brand consistency, and customer-facing communication.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Product marketing, retail insights, packaging briefs, sales coordination.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Assistant Brand Manager, Product Marketing Associate, Category Marketing Executive.

rows.text: Social media, search, paid and organic channels
Aligns brand activity with business objectives

blocks.text: Creative and brand assets
Canva and Adobe Creative Cloud — develop campaign mock-ups, visual concepts, presentations, and creative briefs.
Analytics and reporting
Excel or Google Sheets, Google Analytics, and advertising platform dashboards — assess reach, engagement, conversions, and campaign performance.
Planning and collaboration
Notion, Trello, or similar project-management tools — manage content calendars, campaign timelines, approvals, and team responsibilities.
Audience and market research
Google Trends, surveys, social listening tools, and competitor reviews — identify audience interests, cultural shifts, and market opportunities.
Start with a small toolkit and learn how to use it to solve a marketing problem. Mastering every platform is not necessary for an entry-level role.
Create at least three projects that demonstrate strategic thinking, creative execution, and analytical ability.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Brand positioning for a startup

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Brand strategy
Select a hypothetical or existing small business and define its target audience, competitor landscape, brand promise, positioning, and key messages.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Brand audit, audience personas based on evidence, positioning statement, messaging framework, and sample brand guidelines.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Integrated brand campaign

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Campaign planning
Design a campaign to launch a new product or increase awareness of an existing brand across social media, digital content, and an offline or community channel.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Campaign brief, creative concepts, content calendar, timeline, budget assumptions, and success metrics.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Brand awareness and campaign analysis

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Research and analytics
Use a clearly labelled sample dataset or a small, ethically conducted survey to examine brand awareness, audience preferences, or campaign performance.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Research plan, charts, findings, limitations, and recommendations.

For every case study, explain the business objective, audience, research, strategic choices, creative direction, budget assumptions, and evaluation plan. Distinguish simulated campaign results from actual performance data.

How to improve your chances

items.text: Build a portfolio with brand strategy, campaign planning, and analytics examples.
Learn how to write a clear creative brief and positioning statement.
Practise analysing real campaigns and explaining their target audience and objectives.
Gain practical experience through college societies, student initiatives, internships, or small-business projects.
Apply for brand, marketing, and campaign roles rather than relying only on vacancies with the exact title “Junior Brand Manager.”

rows.text: Brand identity, positioning, equity, and strategy
Content, search, social media, paid advertising
Surveys, sampling, qualitative and quantitative analysis
Creative briefs, strategy decks, stakeholder communication

blocks.text: Choose courses from reputable universities or established training providers. Certifications should support demonstrable work rather than replace it.
Postgraduate study is optional for many brand management roles. It may be useful when aiming for strategic marketing roles or broader business leadership.
MBA in Marketing
Suitable for brand strategy, marketing management, consumer goods, and long-term business leadership. Admissions and recruitment expectations vary by institution.
Master's in Marketing or Strategic Marketing
Focuses on brand positioning, customer strategy, marketing analytics, and integrated campaigns.
Master's in Advertising, Communication, or Media Management
Useful for brand communications, advertising strategy, media planning, and agency careers.
Master's in Consumer Insights, Marketing Analytics, or Market Research
Suitable for candidates who want to combine brand management with customer research and quantitative analysis.

rows.text: Research, content coordination, campaign support, reporting
Junior Brand Manager / Assistant Brand Manager
Coordinate brand plans, agencies, budgets, and campaigns
Own brand strategy, positioning, campaign performance, and budgets
Senior Brand Manager / Group Brand Manager
Manage larger portfolios, product categories, and teams
Set brand direction, manage marketing investments, and lead strategy

blocks.text: Progression depends on company structure, performance, and industry. Some organisations expect prior marketing experience before assigning full brand ownership.
Brand professionals may increasingly work in:

blocks.label: AI-assisted marketing
blocks.text: Using AI for ideation, research synthesis, and creative testing while verifying accuracy and brand suitability.

blocks.label: Creator and community marketing
blocks.text: Building credible relationships with creators and audience communities.

blocks.label: Brand purpose and sustainability
blocks.text: Communicating social or environmental commitments with verifiable evidence.

blocks.label: Personalisation
blocks.text: Tailoring campaigns using customer insights while respecting privacy.

blocks.label: Cultural intelligence
blocks.text: Understanding changing audience values, language, regional contexts, and online communities.

blocks.label: Brand performance analytics
blocks.text: Connecting awareness and engagement with business outcomes.
These are areas to explore, not guarantees of employment growth.
Use this checklist to assess readiness for junior brand management roles.
Brand management readiness tracker
I understand brand positioning, identity, and target audiences.
I can conduct basic competitor and consumer research.
I can write a creative brief and develop campaign messages.
I can plan a content calendar and coordinate campaign tasks.
I can use spreadsheets to analyse campaign performance.
I understand key metrics such as reach, engagement, conversion, and awareness.
I have at least two documented brand or campaign projects.
I can present a marketing recommendation and justify it with evidence.
I have tailored my CV and applications for brand or marketing roles.
Check off each item as you develop the competency. This is a preparation guide, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a strong candidate should be able to:

items.text: Understand brand identity, positioning, and consumer behaviour.
Research audiences and competitors to identify marketing opportunities.
Develop campaign briefs, content plans, and communication strategies.
Coordinate creative work across internal teams and external agencies.
Interpret marketing metrics and recommend evidence-based improvements.
Demonstrate practical ability through internships and portfolio projects.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Learn brand positioning, consumer research, campaign planning, and basic marketing analytics. Build three portfolio projects—a brand strategy, an integrated campaign, and a campaign analysis—then apply for Brand Executive, Marketing Associate, and Junior Brand Manager opportunities.
